articles.titulo: Optimized protocol for single-cell and bulk transcriptomic profiling of stabilized hemocytes frommosquitoes
articles.autores: Saha B, McNinch CM, … Barillas-Mury C (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Insect hemocytes play a crucial role in the innate immune response against pathogens. However, transcriptomic profiling and analysis of hemocytes in insect vectors, such as Anopheles gambiae mosquitoes, are challenging due to their small size, low RNA content, limited numbers, and highly reactive nature.
To address these challenges, we developed a protocol for single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing of stabilized hemocytes from adult female An. gambiae mosquitoes. Immediate stabilization of hemocytes following perfusion prevents transcriptional changes during sample collection and RNA degradation, thereby minimizing technical artifacts. After stabilization, hemocytes are filtered to remove contaminating tissue and ambient RNA introduced by tissue injury during sample collection, enriching for hemocyte-specific transcripts. The stabilized hemocytes can be stored for up to four weeks, allowing for convenient sample storage, transportation, and simultaneous processing of multiple samples, which reduces costs and minimizes batch effects.
Our single-cell RNA sequencing stabilization and processing protocol is compatible with the 10X Genomics platform, yielding high-quality and reproducible data. We demonstrate higher hemocyte recovery compared to other contemporary methods, enabling the identification of rare hemocyte populations. However, this protocol requires further optimization to increase the recovery of small-sized prohemocytes (< 5 μm in diameter). Our bulk mRNA stabilization and hemocyte enrichment protocol yields high-quality, intact RNA, and Illumina bulk mRNA sequencing libraries enable an in-depth investigation of gene expression changes in hemocytes. These protocols significantly improve transcriptomic analysis of hemocytes, which is critical for advancing discoveries in vector biology and disease control. Moreover, the protocol can be applied to other mosquito species and likely many other insects with only minor optimizations.

articles.titulo: A microbial sugar tips the metabolic scales
articles.autores: Weber AM, Spencer SP (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Obesity and metabolic disorders are linked to the microbiome, but the underlying pathways remain poorly defined. In this issue of Cell Host & Microbe, Tan et al. identify a Clostridium immunis-derived exopolysaccharide that reduces interleukin-22 signaling to reshape visceral adipose immunometabolism, and their findings link microbial chemistry to host energy balance.

articles.titulo: Strain-Specific Reduction of Ndel1 Enzymatic Activity During Early Zika Virus Infection in the Neonatal Brain
articles.autores: de Farias IS, Ximenes AP, … Hayashi MAF (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Zika virus (ZIKV) infection during early development is associated with severe neurodevelopmental impairment, including congenital microcephaly, yet the molecular mechanisms linking viral exposure to neuronal dysfunction remain incompletely understood. Ndel1 (nudE neurodevelopment protein 1 like 1) is an oligopeptidase critically involved in neuronal migration, neurite outgrowth, and cytoskeletal dynamics, processes essential for proper brain development. Building on previous observations that Ndel1 enzymatic activity is reduced in ZIKV-infected embryonic and neonatal brains, we investigated whether this modulation represents a conserved host response or a strain-specific molecular effect. Using a neonatal intracerebroventricular infection model in Swiss mice at postnatal day 0, we compared the effects of a Brazilian ZIKV strain (ZIKVBR), an African lineage strain (ZIKVAF), and dengue virus (DENV) on Ndel1 regulation in the brain. We found that Ndel1 enzymatic activity was significantly reduced at early post-infection time points (P3 and P7) exclusively in ZIKVBR-infected animals, whereas ZIKVAF and DENV did not alter enzyme activity relative to controls. Notably, at the earliest timepoint (P3), this reduction occurred in the absence of changes in Ndel1 mRNA expression, indicating an initial post-transcriptional or functional mechanism of regulation, although Ndel1 mRNA expression was also significantly reduced by P7. Although both ZIKV strains induced robust inflammatory gene expression, only ZIKVBR infection resulted in decreased Ndel1 activity, dissociating neuroinflammatory signaling from enzymatic modulation. Importantly, this strain-specific reduction parallels the unique capacity of ZIKVBR to induce microcephaly and supports Ndel1 dysfunction as an early molecular event associated with neurodevelopmental impairment. Together, these findings identify a virus- and strain-specific regulation of a key neuronal enzyme and provide mechanistic insight into the molecular basis of ZIKVBR-associated neurodevelopmental outcomes.

articles.titulo: New sites of vulnerability to stop vivax malaria
articles.autores: Alam N, Higgins MK (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Malaria vaccines based on the PfCSP molecule are now being deployed to prevent infection by the deadly parasite, Plasmodium falciparum. Can we apply the same tricks to stop the second major malaria parasite, Plasmodium vivax? Visweswaren and colleagues studied PvCSP, revealing new sites of vulnerability to target with vaccines.

articles.titulo: Limitation of pantothenate bioavailability inby second-generation pantazines enhances restriction ofdevelopment
articles.autores: Debebe Y, Isoe J, … Luckhart S (13 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Plasmodium parasites require pantothenate (Pan) from their hosts to synthesize coenzyme A (CoA), an essential metabolic cofactor. While blood-stage parasites can utilize both Pan and the immediate CoA precursor phosphopantetheine from mammals to synthesize CoA, mosquito-stage parasites rely critically on insect-derived Pan to synthesize CoA. Mosquito host pantothenate kinase (PanK), the rate-limiting enzyme in CoA biosynthesis, is therefore a promising drug target to reduce Pan bioavailability for parasite development. In support, we previously showed that the mammalian PanK activator PZ-2891 restricts Plasmodium yoelii and Plasmodium falciparum development in Anopheles stephensi. Two second-generation pantazines, PZ-3022 and PZ-3883, with improved stability significantly reduced Pan levels in A. stephensi at different time points post-treatment and had no effect on P. falciparum growth in vitro. In infection assays, mosquitoes provisioned with these pantazines exhibited markedly decreased midgut oocyst and salivary gland sporozoite burdens for both parasite species. These findings confirm that pantazines can effectively impair mosquito-stage parasite development and represent promising transmission-blocking small molecules.
The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-68982-w.

articles.titulo: Elevated synaptic vesicle fusion with impaired activity-dependent neurotransmission in a genomic ferlinopathy model
articles.autores: Randazzo EJ, Rushton E, … Broadie K (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Ferlins are a family of Ca2+/phospholipid-binding C2 domain transmembrane proteins (e.g. Myoferlin, Dysferlin, Otoferlin) mutated in multiple heritable human disease conditions. The unifying function of all Ferlins is Ca2+-dependent vesicle fusion, with roles in muscle formation, membrane repair, and neurotransmission. Drosophila has one well-conserved Ferlin, misfire (mfr), which provides the opportunity to test global Ferlin function via single gene manipulation. We find misfire null mutants form and maintain normal muscles with elevated muscle function. Consistently, we find misfire expressed in motor neurons with loss-of-function elevating synaptic vesicle fusion. Basal neurotransmission is normal at the glutamatergic neuromuscular junction (NMJ) model synapse, but misfire null mutants exhibit progressive synaptic depression with accumulating failures during high-frequency stimulation. We discover that experience-dependent neurotransmission potentiation from chronic neuronal activity elevation is eliminated in the absence of misfire function. These findings suggest neuronal presynaptic vesicle regulation may be the ancestral Ferlin role, similar to Otoferlin function in humans and mouse disease models. Taken together, these results show that misfire modulates synaptic vesicle fusion during neurotransmission and mediates activity-dependent changes in both signaling fidelity and synaptic strength.

articles.titulo: Quinolinic acid as a central immunometabolic mediator of inflammation, neurodegeneration, and disease pathogenesis
articles.autores: Ardah MT, Kubaev A, … Shefali (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Quinolinic acid (QA), a downstream metabolite of the tryptophan-kynurenine pathway, has emerged as a critical immunometabolic molecule linking immune activation, inflammation, and tissue pathology across diverse diseases. Recent evidence demonstrates that altered QA production is associated with chronic inflammatory disorders, neurodegenerative diseases, infections, cancer, and immune dysregulation. In the central nervous system (CNS), pathological accumulation of QA has been associated with excessive N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor activation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and excitotoxicity, contributing to neuronal injury and neuroinflammatory pathology. In inflammatory skin diseases such as psoriasis, microbiota-derived QA modulates NOD-, LRR-, and pyrin domain-containing protein 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome activity through aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR)-dependent mechanisms, highlighting a regulatory role in cutaneous immunity. Studies further identified microglial-derived QA as both a biomarker and mediator of depressive-like behavior, with reductions in QA predicting therapeutic response to ketamine. Beyond inflammatory and neurological disorders, QA and related kynurenine metabolites exhibit anti-proliferative effects in melanoma cells by inducing apoptosis and inhibiting cell-survival signaling pathways. Therapeutic interventions targeting QA-mediated pathways, including microbiota-derived metabolites such as butyrate, have demonstrated neuroprotective and anti-inflammatory effects in experimental models. Understanding the mechanisms governing QA production and signaling may facilitate the development of novel biomarkers and targeted therapies for inflammatory, neurodegenerative, infectious, and malignant diseases.

articles.titulo: Evaluation of the role of P2 neurons on female post-mating changes in sleep and feeding in Drosophila melanogaster
articles.autores: Potdar S, Makhmudova T, … Wolfner MF (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original: In many insects, females exhibit behavioral changes after mating. This plasticity can be mediated by interactions between male-derived seminal fluid proteins (SFPs) and the female nervous system. The Drosophila melanogaster seminal fluid protein Sex Peptide (SP) causes mated females to sleep less during the day and consume more food than unmated females, among other behavioral changes. Although the SP-sensing neural circuits that convey information to the female's brain are known, the downstream neurons that affect post-mating behaviors remain unknown. P2 neurons in the fly's central brain are good candidates for regulating post-mating changes in sleep and food consumption, as they express feeding- and sleep-responsive neuropeptide F (NPF), directly innervate the fly's sleep center (the dorsal fan-shaped body, dFB), and are responsible for social-isolation-induced changes in sleep and food consumption. Using the GAL4/UAS system, we activated or silenced P2 neurons in mated and unmated females. We measured sleep duration using Drosophila Activity Monitors (DAM) and food consumption using Capillary Feeder (CAFE) and blue-dye assays. We found that P2-neurons are not responsible for post-mating changes in sleep and food consumption: mated females slept less during the day and ate more compared to unmated females irrespective of P2 neuron perturbation. Together, these results indicate that P2 neurons are unlikely to be primary downstream neurons through which male-transferred SP regulates post-mating sleep and food consumption. Future studies could determine whether P2 neurons regulate other post-mating behaviors or modulate sleep and feeding behaviors in a context-dependent manner.

articles.titulo: Connectome analysis reveals brain-wide visual processing in
articles.autores: Kim SY, Kim AJ (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Sensory processing relies on a brain-wide network that integrates specialized sensory circuits with the rest of the brain. To understand how this integration shapes visual processing, we used the whole-brain Drosophila melanogaster connectome to analyze the long-range projections that reciprocally connect the optic lobe (OL)-the principal visual center-with the central brain and with the contralateral OL. By quantifying synaptic polarity and connectivity, we classified the projection neurons into feedforward, feedback, and bilateral groups. Feedforward projection neurons form an information bottleneck, consolidating diverse visual features from the OL and distributing them through modular pathways for higher-order processing. Feedback projection neurons densely innervate OL structures, conveying contextual signals from the central brain via recurrent loops formed with specific feedforward projection neurons. Bilateral projection neurons link local visual circuits across the two OLs, providing a substrate for inter-ocular processing. Together, these findings reveal how early visual circuits interface with the rest of the brain, establishing a structural basis for future functional studies on brain-wide visual processing.

v6.resumo: Análise do conectoma de Drosophila classifica neurônios de projeção entre lobo óptico e cérebro central em feedforward, feedback e bilaterais por polaridade sináptica e conectividade.

articles.titulo: Lab-on-chip platform for detection of malaria parasite DNA with graphene transistors
articles.autores: Domingues T, Guerreiro JR, … Borme J (12 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Accurate and sensitive point-of-care diagnosis of malaria, with the ability to distinguish co-infections among Plasmodium species responsible for the disease, is critical for malaria control programs. Species-specific identification is essential for selecting appropriate therapies and preventing recurrence. Moreover, easier and non-invasive infection detection can dramatically reduce the number of infected cases and minimize the pandemic's public health and economic impact. Here, we present a graphene electrolyte-gated field-effect transistor array for a DNA biosensor that enables highly sensitive detection of DNA from five Plasmodium species. The 21-channel chip, grouped into 7 regions for multiplex detection, integrates non-covalently functionalized graphene with ssDNA probes targeting each species. The miniaturized readout platform allows direct and amplification-free measurements upon deposition of small volumes of analyte. Synthetic target DNA was detected in both physiological buffer and 25× diluted saliva with attomolar limit of detection, dynamic ranges spanning more than four orders of magnitude, and sensitivities of ∼16-19 mV/decade. Notably, DNA extracted from P. falciparum cultured parasites, spiked into human saliva, was reliably detected down to ∼10 aM. A mixed-target multiplex experiment on a single chip with 7 functionalized areas demonstrated the absence of target cross-talk. Accelerated ageing experiment at 75% relative humidity or 65 °C showed chips keep their analytical performance. This platform enables direct, amplification-free identification of multiple malaria species, in non-invasive samples. Its combination of sensitivity, specificity, and portability positions this biosensor as a powerful tool for early malaria screening and species differentiation in resource-limited or field settings.

articles.titulo: An integrative model of cholesterol gradients in erythrocytes infected with Plasmodium falciparum
articles.autores: Wumba R (1 autor)
articles.resumo_original: Cholesterol is distributed unevenly across the membranes of erythrocytes infected with Plasmodium falciparum. Earlier imaging and biochemical studies described a relative inward sterol gradient and implicated dilution by parasite-produced lipids. Genetics, localisation, structural studies and cholesterol-analogue efflux assays have since identified PfNCR1 as a determinant of parasite plasma membrane sterol homeostasis. This Review integrates these findings with evidence on host membrane properties, parasitophorous vacuolar membrane formation and membrane expansion during intracellular development. It distinguishes observed redistribution from inferred membrane topology, relative sterol enrichment from absolute cholesterol mass, and transport capacity from the direction and magnitude of flux in infected cells. Cholesterol-dependent invasion phenotypes may reflect membrane mechanics, receptor organisation or cytoskeletal coupling without requiring cholesterol translocation. Likewise, phospholipid expansion can reduce the cholesterol-to-phospholipid ratio without net sterol loss. The resulting partitioning model is an integrative conceptual synthesis, rather than a newly discovered gradient or an experimentally established complete cholesterol-trafficking pathway. Its unresolved steps define opportunities for compartment-resolved measurements and selective therapeutic investigation.

articles.titulo: Plasmodium species positivity rates across regions with different malaria transmission intensities in Mainland Tanzania: Data from a nationwide survey conducted in 2023
articles.autores: Mandai SS, Bakari C, … Ishengoma DS (15 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Although Plasmodium falciparum is the most prevalent and highly virulent species in Sub-Saharan Africa, non-falciparum species are increasingly recognized as a hidden burden. Generally, infections caused by non-falciparum species occur with low parasite densities and often present as co-infections with P. falciparum. These parasites may evade detection by routine diagnostics, complicating malaria case management and control efforts. To investigate the distribution of different Plasmodium parasites, we analysed 5,314 randomly selected samples from 18,969 samples collected across all 26 regions of Mainland Tanzania in 2023. Plasmodium parasites were detected using 18S qPCR. Of the analyzed samples, 52.3% (n = 2,780) were positive for any Plasmodium species. P. falciparum was detected in 51.2% (2,719/5,314), P. malariae in 1.4% (76/5,314), and P. ovale spp. in 1.8% (98/5,314) of the samples. Mixed infections were detected in 2.0% (107/5,314), with P. malariae and P. falciparum in 0.8% (40/5,314), and P. ovale mixed with P. falciparum in 1.1% (61/5,314) of the samples analysed. Among the samples with positive results (n = 2,780), mono-infections were detected at 93.9% (2,612/2,780) for P. falciparum, 1.1% (30/2,780) for P. malariae, and 1.1% (31/2,780) for P. ovale spp., respectively. Unlike P. malariae and P. ovale, P. falciparum infections were significantly influenced by transmission intensities, with the highest odds in regions with high transmission intensities compared to those with low (OR=1.61, p < 0.001), and very low transmission (OR=1.48, p < 0.001). School children had higher odds of P. falciparum infections compared to adults (OR=1.56, p < 0.001) and under-fives (OR=1.47, p < 0.001). Adults were also less likely to have P. malariae infections than schoolchildren (OR= 0.45, p = 0.021).The findings of the first-ever nation-wide survey reveal a high prevalence of P. falciparum, low prevalence of non-falciparum species, and complex species landscape. They underpin the need to expand surveillance systems beyond P. falciparum and adapt interventions to target all Plasmodium species.

articles.titulo: Diagnostic Performance of the Hematology Analyzer XN-31 for Detecting Plasmodium Infections in School-Based Surveillance in Western Kenya
articles.autores: Kagaya W, Tougan T, … Kaneko A (12 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Despite significant progress in malaria control, asymptomatic and submicroscopic infections remain important reservoirs sustaining transmission and are often undetected by conventional microscopy or rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs). The Automated Hematology Analyzer XN-31 (Sysmex, Kobe, Japan) has shown high diagnostic accuracy in clinical settings, but performance under active surveillance, particularly among asymptomatic individuals, has not been evaluated. In this study, we assessed XN-31 using samples from school-based active surveillance in western Kenya, where asymptomatic and submicroscopic infections are highly prevalent. Among 1,237 samples, 564 (45.6%) were positive for Plasmodium spp. by polymerase chain reaction (PCR), including 511 afebrile infections. Using PCR as the reference, XN-31 detected infections with a sensitivity of 70.2%, slightly higher than microscopy (65.1%), and a specificity of 98.4%, higher than RDT (79.8%) and similar to microscopy (98.7%). It detected 43 of 197 submicroscopic infections (21.8%), with a median parasite density of 57 parasites/µL (interquartile range: 38-202). XN-31 identified 11 of 76 mixed infections of Plasmodium falciparum and non-P. falciparum compared with 5 by microscopy and 0 by RDT. Importantly, it also detected 8 of 14 P. falciparum infections suspected to carry hrp2/3 deletions, which caused false-negative RDT results, comparable with microscopy. This is the first study to evaluate XN-31 for detecting asymptomatic infections, non-P. falciparum species, and hrp2/3-deleted parasites, which are key diagnostic challenges in endemic settings. Our findings support the potential of XN-31 as a practical and reliable surveillance tool that bridges between RDTs and PCR for enhanced parasite detection and accelerated malaria control efforts.

articles.titulo: Subsidies for innovative technology adoption: Experimental evidence on malaria in Burkina Faso
articles.autores: Djemaï E, Renard Y (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original: We evaluated both the demand for and impact of a prevention tool against malaria that requires repeated purchase and overcomes the limits of mosquito bed nets. We used a randomized experiment to examine the effects of subsidies for a mosquito repellent ointment that protects against mosquito bites and malaria on product use and malaria cases in Burkina Faso. Around 3100 households were randomly allocated to one of the three experimental groups defined by level of subsidy: 0, 50 or 100%. Subsidies strongly and significantly increase the probability of acquiring a jar of mosquito repellent ointment and using it regularly during the rainy season. We find no substitution with bed nets, but a strong effect on the use of mosquito coils. The treatment effects on usage are heterogeneous, including more positive outcomes for young children as reported by their caregiver. The impact on use continues even after the end of the subsidy, with effects on demand and willingness to pay elicited through a Becker-DeGroot-Marschak approach eight months after the end of the intervention. Our intervention induces a significant reduction in declared malaria occurrence during the rainy season, but no effect at the very end of the rainy season when blood tests were taken. The seemingly discrepancy will be partly explained by timing and sample size.

articles.titulo: A Subnational Age-Structured Mathematical Model of Malaria Transmission and Burden
articles.autores: Kakaï RG (1 autor)
articles.resumo_original: Malaria transmission and burden exhibit substantial spatial and age-related heterogeneity that is often obscured by national-level modeling approaches. In this study, we develop a spatially explicit, age-structured malaria transmission and burden model designed to operate at the subnational scale (Admin-1) while remaining fully consistent with national-level estimates. The model integrates monthly age cohorts (0-100 years), naturally acquired immunity, heterogeneous entomological inoculation rates (EIR), and key non-vaccine interventions, allowing a fine-scale representation of malaria dynamics across space, time, and age. Subnational EIRs are inferred from malaria prevalence in children aged 2-10 years, while age-specific clinical progression and mortality are modeled through immunity-dependent transitions. To ensure national-subnational consistency despite nonlinear transmission dynamics, a parsimonious rescaling framework is introduced, based on time-varying country-level-to-subnational ratios of estimated cases and deaths, ensuring consistency between subnational projections and national burden trajectories. Model calibration is performed using a joint root-mean-square error (RMSE) metric that pools discrepancies across cases and deaths across all administrative units and years. Applying the model to both high- and low-transmission settings (Benin, Burkina-Faso, Ethiopia, and Somalia) successfully reproduces observed national and subnational dynamics, while revealing strong and persistent spatial heterogeneity within countries. The model captures marked geographical gradients in EIR and localized epidemic hotspots. The resulting framework provides a flexible platform for analyzing spatial heterogeneity in malaria transmission, age-specific burden, and intervention impact, and is well-suited for prospective analyses, including the evaluation of vaccination strategies, targeted intervention deployment, and long-term burden projections.

articles.titulo: Forgotten reservoirs: an attempt to revive field research on rodent malaria parasites in their main natural host, the thicket rat Grammomys poensis (formerly Thamnomys rutilans)
articles.autores: Boundenga L, Makanga BK, … Prugnolle F (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Rodent malaria parasites have long served as essential experimental models for understanding human malaria, yet little is known about their ecology and evolution in the wild. The thicket rat Grammomys poensis (formerly Thamnomys rutilans) is considered the main natural host of murine Plasmodium species in Central Africa. This study aimed to establish a long-term field site to investigate Plasmodium-Grammomys interactions under natural conditions in southeastern Gabon. Over a period of 3 years, trapping was conducted across twelve forest fragments in the Batéké Plateau region using both Tomahawk traps and direct collection at nest. Despite an intensive effort (18,000 trap-nights and 1380 nests inspected), only 20 adult Grammomys were captured, all by collection directly at nest. None were infected with Plasmodium as determined by two sensitive nested-PCR assays targeting the cytb gene, suggesting extremely low transmission or absence of parasite circulation in the study system. These results contrast with earlier studies reporting high infection prevalence in Grammomys from other Central African regions. The absence of infection may reflect local extinction of Plasmodium lineages, limited vector exposure due to the absence of species feeding on arboreal rodents, or host resistance. Because the rodent malaria lines currently used as experimental models in laboratories worldwide were isolated decades ago and have since been maintained through serial passage, access to recent field isolates would be highly valuable for capturing contemporary natural diversity and for enhancing the ecological, evolutionary, and biomedical relevance of these model systems. This study highlights both the challenges of studying this host-parasite system in the wild and the possibility that rodent Plasmodium transmission in this system may be more spatially and ecologically constrained than previously assumed.

articles.titulo: Salivary Plasmodium falciparum histidine-rich protein 2 levels are poor predictors of parasite density and clinical malaria status in patients with acute uncomplicated malaria in Chulaimbo, western Kenya
articles.autores: Omingo RA, Ayieko C, … Ogolla S (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Malaria is the leading cause of death and economic burden worldwide. Current diagnostic methods rely on microscopy and blood-based rapid diagnostic tests. A common rapid diagnostic test target is Plasmodium falciparum histidine-rich protein 2 (PfHRP2), a parasite protein released into the host's blood during Plasmodium infection; it has also been detected in saliva, although results have been inconsistent. This pilot study quantified plasma and salivary PfHRP2 antigen levels and assessed their associations with age, parasite density, and clinical malaria status in a malaria-endemic region of western Kenya with high transmission. This pilot study enrolled 34 patients with acute uncomplicated malaria. Paired blood and saliva samples were collected at enrolment, with repeat sampling 4 weeks after treatment. P. falciparum infection was confirmed by light microscopy, and PfHRP2 concentrations were measured using an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Data were analyzed in R version 4.5.2. Spearman's rank correlation and robust linear regression were used to examine the relationship between plasma and salivary P. falciparum antigen levels in individuals with acute malaria and to assess whether PfHRP2 concentrations in either matrix predicted parasite density, clinical malaria status, and age. Salivary PfHRP2 levels did not significantly predict parasite density or age (χ²=0.54, P=0.76). By contrast, plasma PfHRP2 levels strongly predicted both parasite density and age (P=0.034). Plasma and salivary PfHRP2 concentrations were not significantly correlated (ρ=-0.327, P=0.059). Nevertheless, routine measurement of salivary PfHRP2 using more sensitive methods may improve diagnosis and guide treatment management.

articles.titulo: Partial connectivity and fine-scale population structure in Honduran Anopheles albimanus inferred from microsatellite markers
articles.autores: Mejía A, Escobar D, … Fontecha G (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Understanding population connectivity in malaria vectors is important for surveillance in elimination settings, where local dispersal and population subdivision may influence residual transmission and the spread of adaptive traits. Anopheles albimanus is the major malaria vector in Honduras, yet its population structure remains poorly characterized. This study aimed to assess the genetic diversity and population structure of Honduran An. albimanus populations using microsatellite markers.
Adult mosquitoes collected from ten populations across Honduras (n = 176) were genotyped at eight species-specific microsatellite loci. Genetic diversity was estimated using the number of alleles, effective number of alleles, observed and expected heterozygosity, and Wright's fixation index. Population differentiation was evaluated using pairwise FST estimates and analysis of molecular variance (AMOVA). A hierarchical AMOVA was used to assess regional structure, and Bayesian clustering implemented in STRUCTURE was used to infer genetic clusters, with the most likely number of clusters determined using the Evanno ΔK method. Isolation by distance was tested with a Mantel test.
All loci were polymorphic and showed moderate to high genetic diversity (He = 0.513-0.817). Observed heterozygosity was consistently lower than expected, with widespread heterozygote deficits and frequent departures from Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium across populations. Pairwise FST values ranged from 0.008 to 0.195, consistent with heterogeneous levels of genetic connectivity. AMOVA showed that 88% of genetic variation occurred within populations and 12% among populations (PhiPT = 0.117, P < 0.001), consistent with moderate but significant differentiation. Hierarchical AMOVA indicated minimal differentiation between La Mosquitia and the rest of Honduras (PhiRT = 0.012), while Bayesian clustering supported two inferred genetic clusters (K = 2) with evidence of admixture across populations, and Mantel analysis detected no evidence of isolation by distance.
Honduran An. albimanus populations harbor substantial genetic diversity while exhibiting moderate differentiation and fine-scale substructure despite overall connectivity. These findings are consistent with a model of partial connectivity shaped primarily by local population-level processes and illustrate the utility of microsatellite markers for detecting contemporary population structure relevant to malaria vector surveillance and control in elimination settings. Given the limited number of loci and the modest, cross-sectional sample, the structure reported here should be regarded as a conservative estimate of underlying population subdivision.

v6.resumo: Microssatélites em 176 An. albimanus de dez populações de Honduras mostram conectividade parcial e estrutura populacional em escala fina.

articles.titulo: Factors associated with TAK-003 dengue vaccine acceptance among Thai adults using the Health Belief Model and Theory of Planned Behavior in a tertiary care hospital
articles.autores: Thanatepaisansakun T, Homsanit M, … Phatharodom P (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Although the live-attenuated tetravalent dengue vaccine (TAK-003) is now available in Thailand, evidence on the behavioral determinants of its acceptance remains limited. We assessed TAK-003 vaccine acceptance, identified factors associated with acceptance using the Health Belief Model and Theory of Planned Behavior frameworks, and evaluated willingness to pay. We conducted a cross-sectional survey from December 2025 to February 2026. Thai adults aged 18-60 years who had never received a dengue vaccine were included and recruited through convenience sampling at Siriraj Hospital, Bangkok. Factors associated with vaccine acceptance were identified using multivariable binary logistic regression. A total of 448 participants were included, of whom 46.7% (n = 209) accepted the TAK-003 vaccine. In the adjusted model, participants aged 50-60 years (adjusted Odd ratio (aOR) = 2.61, 95% CI: 1.33-5.11), those with a history of dengue infection (aOR = 2.61, 95% CI: 1.56-4.35), greater perceived susceptibility (aOR = 1.57, 95% CI: 1.02-2.41), greater perceived benefits (aOR = 2.57, 95% CI: 1.44-4.60), stronger cues to action (aOR = 2.33, 95% CI: 1.20-4.55), and more positive attitudes toward the vaccine (aOR = 1.74, 95% CI: 1.06-2.84) were significantly associated with vaccine acceptance. Approximately 42.9% (n = 192) of participants were willing to pay ≤500 THB per vaccine dose. These findings may inform local strategies for communicating dengue risk and vaccine benefits and addressing affordability of TAK-003 vaccination.

articles.titulo: Designing a multi-epitope subunit vaccine against chikungunya virus using immunoinformatics and molecular simulation approaches
articles.autores: Ahmed SF, Mondal A, … Verma AK (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Chikungunya is a mosquito-borne viral illness that is responsible for increased rates of infection and major public health consequences, but no approved vaccine is available yet. This research employed an integrated approach of immunoinformatics and structural vaccinology to develop a promising multi-epitope subunit vaccine candidate. This study focused on the conserved structural polyprotein (NP_690589) for the purpose of epitope predictions. After strict filtering for high antigenicity, safety, and excellent conservation (> 90%), 9 CTL epitopes, 8 HTL epitopes, and 5 B-cell epitopes were selected. The ultimate vaccine formulation, associated with beta-defensin-3 as an adjuvant, demonstrated favorable physicochemical characteristics, robust antigenicity (score 0.7317), and an anticipated global population coverage of 91.79%. Molecular docking revealed very stable binding to human TLR4 and TLR2. TLR4 was further confirmed by 100 ns MD simulation. Thereafter, an immune simulation study revealed the potentiality of the vaccine to augment both innate and adaptive immune responses. Codon optimization was done for efficient expression in E. coli. The mRNA of the proposed vaccine exhibited stability in in vivo conditions. This in silico-designed vaccine candidate suggests it is highly immunogenic, physically stable, and widely protective. It is a strong candidate that now needs experimental validation to move toward preclinical testing.
The online version contains supplementary material available at 10.1038/s41598-026-50862-y.

articles.titulo: Complex non-transmission and widespread insecticide resistance sustain hyperendemic malaria in Penka-Michel, a focus of the Cameroon highlands
articles.autores: Kiam BC, Ibrahima I, … Nsango SE (15 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
A 12-month longitudinal entomological study (September 2023-August 2024) in the Western Highlands of Cameroon (Penka-Michel) investigated malaria transmission dynamics and insecticide resistance markers, including target-site resistance (L1014F, N1575Y, G119S-Ace1) and metabolic resistance (E205D-CYP6P3, L119F-GSTe2, CYP6P9a/b) mutations. Malaria transmission was driven by the coexistence of three species: Anopheles funestus (43.7%), Anopheles gambiae (42.9%), and Anopheles ziemanni (13.5%). The study site was hyperendemic with an annual Entomological Inoculation Rate (EIR) of 839.5 infective-bites/human/year. Plasmodium falciparum predominated at 51.9% (68/131), though a significant non-falciparum burden was observed (P. malariae: 14.5%, 19/131; P. ovale: 15.3%, 20/131), including mixed infections (18.3%, 24/131). Anopheles funestus was the principal driver (Infection Rate, IR, of 7.8%) for P. falciparum and P. ovale curtisi, which peaked in the later rainy season (November). Anopheles gambiae (IR=5.4%) primarily vectored P. malariae, maintaining a sustained peak during the dry season (January). Widespread insecticide resistance was marked by high frequencies of target-site and metabolic resistance markers. Possible associations were observed between L119F-GSTe2 mutations with P. ovale curtisi transmission (IRR=1.15, p=0.03), and L1014F-kdr mutation with P. malariae (IRR=2.2, p=0.04). These dynamics underscore the intricate nature of a multifaceted, species-diverse system, where seasonal vector efficiency and insecticide resistance perpetuate the hyperendemicity of the frequently disregarded non-falciparum malaria species.
The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-69358-w.

articles.titulo: The prediction of Aedes mosquito abundance using remote sensing and machine learning in Harris County, Texas
articles.autores: Li H, Zhou J, … Gunter SM (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Vector-borne diseases, particularly those transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, remain a major public health challenge globally, with species like Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus as primary vectors of dengue, chikungunya, and Zika viruses. The management of these mosquitoes is complicated by their adaptability to urban environments and the resource limitations of mosquito control programs. This study presents a proof-of-concept approach to improve Aedes surveillance and control by integrating remote sensing data and machine learning techniques. We used Sentinel-2 satellite imagery and environmental data to predict Aedes abundance across Harris County, Texas, incorporating both weather and socioeconomic features into predictive models. Using XGBoost, a machine learning algorithm, we identified high-risk areas for mosquito abundance with increased accuracy over traditional methods. This study demonstrates the potential of combining remote sensing with machine learning for enhancing mosquito surveillance programs, offering an innovative new strategy to improve vector control and mitigate the spread of mosquito-borne diseases. Future research should explore broader geographic applications and additional environmental variables to further refine predictive models.
The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-64249-6.

articles.resumo_original: Dengue is a febrile illness caused by four distinct dengue viruses (DENV-1, DENV-2, DENV-3, and DENV-4). The virus is transmitted by infected Aedes mosquitoes (1). In 2025, several countries and territories in the Western Pacific Region experienced dengue outbreaks (2), and on June 20, 2025, American Samoa, a territory of the United States located in the south Pacific Ocean, reported its first positive dengue test result in 2025. Two weeks later, on July 8, American Samoa declared a public health emergency after identifying six dengue cases, including two locally acquired cases and four associated with travel to neighboring Samoa, where a large dengue outbreak was ongoing (3,4). Recent dengue outbreaks in American Samoa were associated with DENV-4 (2009), DENV-3 (2015), and DENV-2 (2016-2018) (5). After the 2016-2018 outbreak, American Samoa implemented confirmatory laboratory dengue testing on the island.

articles.titulo: A scoping review of naturally occurring Chandipura virus in animal hosts and arthropod vectors
articles.autores: Touma D, Sandhu JS, … Brookes VJ (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Chandipura virus (CHPV), an emerging rhabdovirus endemic to India, causes acute encephalitis, primarily in children. In 2024, India experienced its worst CHPV outbreak in 20 years (245 cases, 33% fatal). Sandflies (family Psychodidae, subfamily Phlebotominae) are considered the primary vectors, but experimental evidence suggests mosquitoes can support infection under laboratory conditions. Animal host species involved in natural transmission remain unknown. We conducted this PRISMA-guided scoping review to identify evidence of natural CHPV infection in animals and arthropods to assess surveillance and emergence potential. Scopus, PubMed, Web of Science and Google Scholar, and three Indian databases (Shodhganga, Krishikosh and CeRA), were searched using predefined terms. Eligible studies included peer-reviewed primary research detecting evidence of CHPV infection (antigen, RNA or antibodies) in arthropods and non-human vertebrate hosts, excluding experimental infection studies. Two reviewers independently screened records, then extracted data on species, location, detection methods and prevalence or seroprevalence. Of 451 screened records (747 total with 296 duplicates removed), 11 met the inclusion criteria. Direct evidence of CHPV infection was reported in phlebotomine sandflies in India, Senegal and Kenya, with low inferred infection prevalence even in outbreak-associated investigations. No evidence was found of natural CHPV infection in wild mosquito or tick populations. Indirect evidence of CHPV exposure (neutralising antibodies) was reported in several livestock species (cattle, buffalo, sheep, goats, pigs), dogs and wild toque macaques, and virus was isolated from a single African hedgehog. In conclusion, direct detection of CHPV in sandflies is consistent with their role as vectors, yet the broader animal host range, their role in virus maintenance and amplification, and the ecological drivers of transmission are incompletely understood. This review highlights the need for integrated One Health surveillance and targeted host-vector studies as globalisation and environmental change promote the spread and redistribution of competent vectors.

articles.titulo: Molecular confirmation of Anopheles gambiae sensu stricto (Diptera: Culicidae) at multiple locations in southern Ethiopia
articles.autores: Zhong D, Zhou G, … Yan G (11 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Anopheles gambiae sensu stricto Giles is a major malaria vector in sub-Saharan Africa but has been infrequently documented in Ethiopia, where Anopheles arabiensis has historically been considered the predominant member of the Anopheles gambiae complex. We investigated Anopheles species composition during larval surveillance at 8 sites in southern and southwestern Ethiopia during 2025-2026. Larvae species were identified using multiplex PCR and species-specific TaqMan quantitative PCR (qPCR), with selected specimens further characterized by internal transcribed spacer 2 (ITS2) and mitochondrial cytochrome c oxidase subunit 1 (cox1) sequencing. Among 503 larvae from 94 molecularly sampled aquatic habitats, 216 were identified as An. arabiensis, 158 as An. stephensi, and 40 as An. gambiae s.s.; 89 remained unresolved. Anopheles gambiae s.s. was detected at 4 geographically distinct sites: Soddo, Birbir, Dila, and Arba Minch. All 40 specimens were concordantly identified by multiplex PCR and qPCR, and their identical ITS2 sequences matched An. gambiae s.s. reference sequences from Kenya and Tanzania. Anopheles gambiae s.s. was detected in 18 molecularly sampled habitats (12 rural and 6 peri-urban), whereas An. stephensi was detected in 35 habitats (27 urban, 6 peri-urban, and 2 rural). Because sampling was not designed to estimate relative abundance or habitat preference, these ecological patterns are descriptive. These findings confirm An. gambiae s.s. at multiple locations in southern Ethiopia and support the use of molecular identification for improved characterization of malaria vector species composition.

articles.titulo: Virological surveillance of chikungunya in Burkina Faso in 2024
articles.autores: Kagoné H, Tranchot-Diallo J, … Kagoné TS (23 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Chikungunya is an emerging arbovirus disease transmitted by mosquitoes of the genus Aedes, mainly Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus. Since it was first identified in Tanzania in 1952, the virus has caused numerous epidemics around the world. Despite arbovirus surveillance since 2017 through sentinel and non-sentinel sites in Burkina Faso, the National Reference Laboratory for Viral Hemorrhagic Fevers (LNR-FHV) confirmed the first cases of Chikungunya in 2023. In spite of a few cases detected in 2024, data on the circulation of the virus remain fragmentary. The objective of this study is to document cases of Chikungunya in 2024 in Burkina Faso.
From January to December 2024, the LNR-FHV received and analyzed 5,821 serum samples from suspected or probable arbovirus cases collected from various sentinel sites, health districts, and medical facilities, using real-time RT-PCR. The tests were performed using a triplex kit (ZDC), a reagent that allows the simultaneous detection of the RNA of three arboviruses (chikungunya, dengue, and Zika).
Of the 5,821 samples tested, 107 cases were confirmed, representing a percentage of positivity case of 1.84%. Women accounted for 54.20% of confirmed cases. The most affected age group was 25-64 years old, with a frequency of 50.47%. No significant association was found between gender (p = 0.28), age (p = 0.73), and infection. The peak was observed in October, accounting for 34.58% of confirmed cases. The Kadiogo region was the most affected by the infection.
This study confirms the circulation of the chikungunya virus in Burkina Faso and highlights the importance of strengthening surveillance, improving diagnosis, and intensifying vector control to prevent outbreaks and better understand the dynamics of the virus.

articles.titulo: Global disparities in dengue, climate, and extreme weather research: a bibliometric analysis of alignment with disease burden and climate-driven vector suitability
articles.autores: Ai C, Teng Y, … Liu Q (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Dengue is a climate-sensitive vector-borne disease that imposes a substantial public health burden in tropical and subtropical regions. Temperature, rainfall, and extreme weather can affect mosquito ecology, human exposure, and the environmental suitability for transmission. This study characterized the global research landscape of dengue and extreme weather and examined whether country-level research output corresponded to dengue burden and climate-driven vector suitability.
The Web of Science Core Collection was searched on 22 May 2026. Publication trends, collaboration networks, journals, authors, co-cited references, citation bursts, keyword patterns, and thematic evolution were examined using CiteSpace, VOSviewer, and the bibliometrix R package. Country-level publication output was linked to estimates from the Global Burden of Disease 2023 dataset, the socio-demographic index for 2021, and mean index-p values for 1990-2022. Associations between publication output and dengue burden were assessed using Spearman's rank correlation among countries classified as dengue-endemic.
A total of 290 publications from 2008 to 2026 met the eligibility criteria. Annual publication output increased overall and remained comparatively high after 2020. The United States contributed the largest number of publications, followed by China, the United Kingdom, Australia, and Brazil. The literature connected tropical medicine and infectious disease epidemiology with environmental health, climate science, vector ecology, modeling, and public health. Major themes included climate change, temperature, rainfall, the El Niño-Southern Oscillation, extreme weather, Aedes vectors, transmission modeling, risk prediction, and early warning. Among 80 countries classified as dengue-endemic, publication output was positively correlated with the age-standardized incidence rate (ASIR) in 2023 (Spearman's ρ = 0.32, P = 0.004, n = 80) and the disability-adjusted life-year (DALY) rate in 2023 (ρ = 0.36, P < 0.001, n = 80). In contrast, its association with the estimated annual percentage change (EAPC) in ASIR from 1990 to 2023 was not statistically significant (ρ = 0.20, P = 0.070, n = 80). Several dengue-endemic countries with comparatively high disease burden or long-term climate-driven vector suitability had no eligible Web of Science-indexed publications in the present dataset.
Research on dengue and extreme weather has expanded, and publication output showed modest positive associations with contemporary dengue burden among dengue-endemic countries. However, research output was not significantly associated with the long-term trend in dengue incidence, and substantial geographic disparities remained. The separate assessment of burden, research output, and climate-driven vector suitability identified geographic areas that may warrant closer consideration when research capacity, surveillance support, and equitable international partnerships are developed.

articles.titulo: Zoonoses and arboviruses: clinical impact of climate change
articles.autores: Membrillo-de-Novales FJ, Arce-García O, … Rodríguez-Morales AJ (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Climate change, global travel, and rapid urbanization are profoundly altering the epidemiology of infectious diseases. Rising global temperatures and the proliferation of ecotones have increased human-animal contact, driving the emergence of zoonoses and arboviruses. In Europe, the geographic expansion of vectors such as Aedes spp. and ticks has led to unprecedented outbreaks of Dengue, West Nile Virus, and Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever. This narrative review explores the clinical and public health impacts of these shifting paradigms, highlighting the urgent need to address Neglected Tropical Diseases and to adopt a global "One Health" approach to mitigate future health threats.

articles.titulo: Severe dengue in an adolescent with graves' disease: a case report
articles.autores: Lai L, Huang Q, … Wang C (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Dengue fever is a mosquito-borne viral disease with clinical manifestations ranging from mild febrile to severe disease. Mild cases may present with fever only, whereas severe cases can progress to life-threatening hemorrhage or shock. The coexistence of severe dengue and Graves' disease in adolescents is rarely reported. Because the two conditions may share clinical manifestations, their coexistence can complicate diagnosis and management.
We report the case of a 17-year-old female adolescent with severe dengue and preexisting Graves' disease. The patient had an 8-year history of preexisting Graves' disease with hyperthyroidism. In June 2025, she traveled to Yunnan Province and reported mosquito bites. In July, the patient travelled to Haikou. One week later, she developed acute nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and persistent fever. The patient presented to a local hospital on July 15, 2025. Laboratory testing was positive for nonstructural protein 1 antigen and viral nucleic acid, confirming dengue virus infection. Serum complete blood counts showed progressive leukopenia and thrombocytopenia. Endocrinological assessment revealed a suppressed thyroid-stimulating hormone level, elevated free thyroid hormone levels, positive thyroid antibodies, and markedly elevated thyroid peroxidase antibodies (>1000 IU/mL). These findings were consistent with severe dengue, active Graves' disease, and Hashimoto's thyroiditis. The patient received comprehensive supportive care, including continuous hemodynamic monitoring, gastric mucosal protection, antipyretic therapy, cautious fluid resuscitation, and careful management of the electrolyte and acid-base balance. Methimazole was administered to control thyrotoxicosis. Her clinical condition gradually improved, and she was discharged in stable condition with endocrinology follow-up arranged.

articles.titulo: An explainable machine-learning framework for seasonal early warning of West Nile virus using predictive climate data
articles.autores: Pappa A, Kioutsioukis I (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Reliable early-warning systems capable of forecasting West Nile virus (WNV) outbreaks months before the transmission season remain limited. We developed an explainable machine-learning framework that uses seasonal climate forecasts rather than in-season reanalysis, combined with epidemiological, climatic, hydroclimatic, demographic, land-cover, and spatial predictors. The model was independently evaluated under real-world conditions at municipal and regional scales in Greece during 2022-2025 and across 887 areas in 14 European countries during 2022-2024. Explainability analysis identified epidemiological memory, seasonal temperature, hydroclimatic persistence, and environmental suitability as key determinants of outbreak risk. Across Europe, the model detected 89% of outbreaks in previously unaffected areas, demonstrating transferability and the potential of integrating prospective climate information with epidemiological history to support targeted WNV surveillance, vector control, and public health preparedness. Skill losses were not attributable to climate forecast errors, highlighting the value of higher frequency epidemiological surveillance (mosquitoes, sentinels) data, which are rarely publicly available.

articles.titulo: Optimising dengue preparedness and response capacity in the WHO African Region: insights from 7-1-7 timeliness metrics assessment
articles.autores: Otshudiema JO, Chanda E, … Gueye AS (29 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Dengue outbreaks are an increasing public health concern in the WHO African Region, where timely detection, notification and early response are essential for outbreak control. The 7-1-7 framework provides operational targets for detecting a suspected outbreak within 7 days of emergence, notifying public health authorities within 1 day of detection and completing defined early response actions within 7 days of notification. This study aimed to describe dengue outbreak timeliness across selected countries in the WHO African Region and to identify operational bottlenecks and enablers using the 7-1-7 framework.
We conducted a retrospective descriptive assessment of dengue outbreak detection, notification and early response in seven purposively selected WHO African Region countries affected during 2023-2024. The country was the unit of analysis. Data were compiled from Ministry of Health surveillance sources, dengue incident management records, situation reports, country presentations, WHO African Regional Office dengue incident management databases, 7-1-7/Early Action Review templates and validation workshops. Country-level 2022 arboviral preparedness assessment scores were used as contextual baseline information. Timeliness intervals were summarised using descriptive statistics, including medians, ranges and proportions meeting 7-1-7 targets.
Across the seven countries, the median time to detection was 3 days, the median time to notification was 0 days and the median time to completion of all defined early response actions was 35 days. Six of seven countries met the ≤7-day detection target, four of seven met the ≤1-day notification target and no country fully met the ≤7-day early response completion target. Detection and notification were therefore generally more timely than completion of all early response actions. The most frequently reported bottlenecks related to laboratory and diagnostic capacity, coordination, case management, community engagement, vector control and response resources. Descriptive patterns suggested variation in timeliness across countries; however, the small number of country-level observations precluded confirmatory statistical inference.
This retrospective country-level assessment suggests that the 7-1-7 framework can help identify operational delays in dengue outbreak response in selected WHO African Region countries. Findings should be interpreted as descriptive and hypothesis-generating because of purposive sampling, retrospective data reconstruction, ecological country-level analysis and the small number of observations. Strengthening data systems, response coordination, laboratory and clinical capacities, community engagement, vector control and documentation of early response actions may improve future dengue outbreak preparedness and response.

articles.titulo: A climate-driven mechanistic transmission model to characterize dengue epidemiology in Dhaka, Bangladesh
articles.autores: Paul KK, Regan DG, … Gray RT (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Dengue is a major public health concern in tropical and sub-tropical areas of the world. Dengue virus is transmitted to humans primarily by female Aedes aegypti mosquitoes and its epidemiology is heavily influenced by the climate. We developed a mechanistic compartmental model to characterize how climate and the evolution of population-level immunity influence changes in the epidemiology of dengue. The model explicitly incorporates aquatic and adult stages of the mosquito vector and cross-immunity (to another serotype) to better represent the transmission of dengue compared to previous models. It incorporates parameters related to mosquito development, behaviour, and mortality that are dependent on temperature, rainfall, and humidity. We calibrated the model to available dengue seroprevalence estimates for Dhaka, Bangladesh as it is a well-observed densely populated endemic area for dengue and will be strongly impacted by climate change. We then simulated dengue epidemiology for the period of 1995-2014 and compared the simulation output with available epidemiologic data. The model produced repeating annual outbreaks of dengue with strong seasonality, as observed in the dengue case reports for Dhaka. The median number of annual dengue infections produced by the model was 1.6 million (IQR: 0.6-2.3 million) and the median of the annual daily peak size of dengue infections was 24,121 (IQR: 7,807-39,308) across the simulations. These figures while exceeding reported cases in Dhaka, which do not include asymptomatic infections or cases not seeking healthcare, align with previous estimates. The modelled seroprevalence of 62% (IQR: 58-75%) aligned with survey results from Dhaka. In most model simulations, dengue infections occurred during August to December with the median peak occurring in October. The model outputs demonstrated a high degree of conformity to the reported data in terms of seasonality, and seroprevalence, indicating that the model provides a good representation of overall dengue epidemiology in Dhaka. By accounting for climate variables, host immunity, and their interplay, our model is well-suited for evaluating the long-term impact of climate change on dengue transmission in Dhaka and other settings where climate and epidemiological data are available.

articles.titulo: Immune impairments in the offspring following parental cadmium exposure in Drosophila melanogaster
articles.autores: Shaikh FH, D'Souza LC, … Sharma A (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Chronic exposure to environmental toxicants, such as cadmium (Cd), poses significant health risks that may extend across generations. However, studies demonstrating immune dysregulation following parental exposure to Cd are limited. Hence, this study aimed to investigate the intergenerational impact of chronic parental Cd exposure on immune homeostasis using Drosophila melanogaster as a model. Parental flies were exposed to two concentrations of cadmium chloride (2 and 20 μg/mL) for 20 days, and multiple endpoints, including the hematopoietic progenitor population, differentiated hemocytes (Drosophila immune cells), circulatory hemocytes and their function (phagocytotic and clotting time), expression of pattern recognition receptors, and antimicrobial peptides, were assessed in their unexposed progeny. The results showed that offspring of chronically Cd-exposed parents experienced a reduced hemocyte population, exhibiting an accumulation of hemocyte progenitors in the lymph glands (Drosophila hematopoietic organs). Reduction in the total number of circulatory hemocytes, decreased phagocytic activity, prolonged clotting time, and downregulation of key pattern recognition receptors (Toll-9, Peptidoglycan Recognition Protein LC (PGRP-LC)) were also observed. Likewise, humoral immunity was also compromised, as evidenced by reduced levels of antimicrobial peptides (Diptericin, Attacin, Drosomycin). Overall, these results suggest that prolonged parental Cd exposure significantly impairs the cellular and humoral immune responses of offspring, indicating its potential to induce intergenerational immune perturbations.

articles.titulo: One battle after another: orthoflavivirus receptors start to be revealed
articles.autores: Cong Y, Wang W, … Tan X (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Orthoflaviviruses, members of the genus Orthoflavivirus in the family Flaviviridae, include major arthropod-borne pathogens, such as dengue, Zika, yellow fever, Japanese encephalitis, and West Nile viruses. Their continued emergence and re-emergence are shaped by viral evolution, vector ecology, urbanization, climate change, human mobility, and uneven population immunity. Understanding the infection biology of these viruses will pave the way for developing therapeutic and preventive countermeasures. Recent discoveries identifying members of the low-density lipoprotein receptor family as functional entry receptors for yellow fever virus and tick-borne encephalitis virus have reshaped our understanding of orthoflavivirus entry. In this review, we analyze these new developments in the context of prior knowledge of orthoflavivirus receptors. We also discuss the evolutionary implications of receptor usage and how receptor identification may accelerate the development of antiviral drugs and vaccines. We propose a framework of orthoflavivirus-host receptor evolution that can be tested experimentally and can guide the development of prediction tools for comprehensive viral receptor usage.

articles.titulo: Single-cell transcriptomic analysis of the immune response to CHIKV infection
articles.autores: Huang P, Wang H, … Pan W (10 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
The Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), a re-emerging mosquito-borne alphavirus, is responsible for acute febrile illness and severe polyarthralgia. Although both innate and adaptive immune responses influence the disease outcomes, the detailed cellular immunopathogenesis of CHIKV in peripheral blood is not yet fully elucidated.
We profiled PBMCs from 29 patients with acute CHIKV infection and 10 controls via single-cell RNA sequencing. Between-group analyses treated donors as biological replicates, incorporating pseudobulk differential expression analysis as well as donor-level comparisons of pathway scores and cell proportions. Orthogonal validation was performed using qPCR and ELISA, and an exploratory analysis was conducted on a publicly available DENV dataset.
Interferon-response signatures were upregulated across the majority of PBMC populations, with particularly prominent signals observed in monocytes and NK cells. Differences in relative cell composition were detected in descriptive statistics, but did not retain statistical significance after donor-level multiple testing correction. B-cell immunoglobulin isotypes varied across cell subsets, and their transcripts did not allow determination of antigen specificity. Cross-study analysis of DENV did not support the quantitative conclusion that the CHIKV-induced immune response is stronger.
Acute CHIKV infection is associated with a broad interferon-stimulated transcriptional program in PBMCs. Conclusions drawn from cross-sectional and cross-study comparisons require cautious interpretation.

articles.titulo: Accumulation of Polyphosphate Inhibits Biofilm Formation in Mycobacteria by Activating RegX3 to Reduce Intracellular c-di-GMP Levels
articles.autores: Huang T, Zhen J, … Xie J (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Mycobacterium tuberculosis can persist in the host for prolonged periods. Biofilm formation represents a key strategy that promotes bacterial persistence, enhances antibiotic resistance, and facilitates immune evasion. Thus, targeting biofilm formation holds significant therapeutic potential for tuberculosis. Exopolyphosphatase 1 (PPX1), highly conserved among mycobacteria, hydrolyzes inorganic polyphosphate. Although changes in polyphosphate levels are known to influence mycobacterial biofilm formation, the underlying mechanism remains unclear. In this study, using a Mycobacterium smegmatis model strain, we found that the level of polyphosphate in the Δppx1 mutant significantly increases, concomitant with impaired biofilm formation. Further investigation revealed that elevated polyphosphate enhances the transcriptional activity of the transcription factor RegX3, which in turn represses biofilm formation. Mechanistically, activated RegX3 directly binds to and upregulates the dcpA gene, encoding a bifunctional enzyme that lowers intracellular cyclic di-GMP levels. This reduction ultimately perturbs cell wall lipid synthesis and compromises biofilm formation. In summary, this work reveals a signaling pathway through which polyphosphate governs biofilm formation in M. smegmatis.

articles.titulo: Polyphosphate Metabolism and Pyoverdine Production Modulate Zebrafish Survival Following Larval Immersion Exposure to Pseudomonas aeruginosa
articles.autores: Ortiz-Severín J, Lecaros C, … Chávez FP (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Bacterial metabolism is increasingly recognized as a central determinant of bacterial virulence, linking the physiological state of the pathogen to its ability to survive and damage the host. Understanding how bacterial metabolism shapes virulence requires models that are both biologically informative and experimentally accessible. Here, we used zebrafish (Danio rerio) larvae for static immersion assays as a simple model to study Pseudomonas aeruginosa host-pathogen interactions and virulence regulation. Using this approach, we show that disruption of polyphosphate (polyP) synthesis by loss of ppk1 gene (Δppk1) leads to marked attenuation of virulence, whereas interrupting ppk2 gene (Δppk2) results in increased mortality in zebrafish larvae. Phenotypic assays and quantitative proteomics revealed that loss of polyP impairs siderophore production, with minimal effects on other canonical virulence factors. Consistently, a pyoverdine-deficient mutant (ΔpvdF) exhibited reduced virulence in zebrafish, validating the capacity of the zebrafish model to functionally resolve key virulence factors. Together, our results highlight polyphosphate metabolism as a central regulator of P. aeruginosa virulence and position zebrafish immersion assays as an efficient and ethically aligned alternative to mammalian models for studying bacterial pathogenesis.

articles.titulo: Detection ofandthroughout the life cycle of Colombian populations of: evidence of potential vertical transmission
articles.autores: Yepes-Acevedo AJ, Lopez-Rivera N, … Saldamando-Benjumea CI (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Spodoptera frugiperda, commonly known as the fall armyworm (FAW), is a pest of great economic importance in corn. The species has recently expanded from the Western Hemisphere to Africa, Asia, and Oceania, increasing its global impact. FAW has diverged into two strains, corn and rice, which differ in genetics, reproductive isolation, resistance to insecticides and to Bacillus thuringiensis, and, more recently found, in their microbiota. Endosymbionts such as Arsenophonus and Spiroplasma have been detected using next-generation sequencing (NGS) of the 16S rRNA gene. However, information on additional endosymbionts and their transmission dynamics remains limited. Therefore, the objectives of this study were to (i) evaluate the presence of endosymbionts such as Arsenophonus, Cardinium, Spiroplasma, and Wolbachia as well as the intracellular parasite Microsporidia, throughout the life cycle of both strains of S. frugiperda, (ii) assess their potential vertical transmission, and (iii) examine possible associations between these symbionts and life-history traits in this insect.
Larvae were sampled from corn and rice fields in central and eastern Colombia. Laboratory colonies of the corn and rice strains of S. frugiperda were maintained under controlled conditions. Strain identity was confirmed using diagnostic molecular markers (MspI, SacI, FR). Within each strain, one-to-one crosses were performed to construct life cycle tables and estimate life-history traits components. DNA was subsequently extracted from parental individuals and from eggs, larvae, pupae, and adults. Following extraction, conventional and real-time polymerase chain reaction (PCR) using an intercalating dye were conducted to identify the genera Arsenophonus, Cardinium, Spiroplasma, and Wolbachia, the intracellular parasite Microsporidia and positive amplifications were confirmed by Sanger sequencing.
Arsenophonus was detected exclusively in the corn strain using conventional PCR and confirmed by Sanger sequencing. Additionally, Spiroplasma was detected in both strains using real-time PCR using an intercalating dye. The detection of these endosymbionts across developmental stages is consistent with, vertical transmission. Differences in life-history traits components were observed between the two strains, but no clear association was detected between these differences and the presence of either endosymbiont under the conditions evaluated. These results highlight the need for further studies to evaluate the potential role of endosymbionts in the biology of this pest and to further on to better understand their transmission dynamics and possible ecological interactions.
