articles.titulo: Sparse gut microbiomes in solitary bees and wasps.
articles.autores: Saiyawong JNS, Watrous KM, … Hammer TJ (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Bees and wasps are ecologically vital, but many species are declining owing to anthropogenic stressors. Social bees harbour host-specific and dense gut microbiomes that affect their resilience to stress. However, there are tens of thousands of other bee and wasp species that vary in sociality and diet (including pollen-feeding and predatory guilds), traits known to influence host-microbe symbioses. The role of gut microbes in the biology of these species is largely unknown. Here, we measured the composition and absolute abundance of bacterial communities in adult metasomas across 61 genera and 14 families of field-collected bees, predatory wasps and pollen wasps. We found that solitary bees and both wasp guilds harbour distinct bacterial taxa and lower bacterial abundances as compared with social bees. Bacterial abundances also varied extensively among and within genera of solitary bees, with little variation explained by body size, diet breadth or nesting ecology. Furthermore, microbiome composition was only weakly differentiated among solitary bees and the two wasp groups, even when comparing herbivorous (pollen-feeding) and omnivorous taxa. We suggest that the sparse and somewhat stochastic microbiomes of solitary bees and wasps reflect weak host dependence on microbially mediated functions, a trait that may influence their responses to environmental change.

articles.titulo: Parathyroid hormone, vitamin D, and general and abdominal adiposity in bariatric surgery candidates: A cross-sectional analysis of the Tehran Obesity Treatment Study.
articles.autores: Aghajanian S, Barzin M, … Bakhtiyari M (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Obesity is commonly accompanied by low circulating 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D], potentially because of volumetric dilution, adipose distribution, and obesity-related changes in 25(OH)D metabolism. Parathyroid hormone (PTH) and 25(OH)D are linked through calcium-phosphate homeostasis and renal conversion of 25(OH)D to calcitriol, but whether 25(OH)D statistically accounts for the association between PTH and adiposity remains uncertain. The data derived from the baseline visit of 4822 participants Tehran Obesity Treatment Study was used to examine the relationship between PTH and 25(OH)D with obesity using regression models. Furthermore, a mediation analysis using potential-outcomes framework was carried out using the aforementioned factors to obtain direct effect of PTH and mediated effect of 25(OH)D on body mass index (BMI) and waist circumference (WC). Higher PTH and lower 25(OH)D were associated with greater adiposity. Compared with the lowest PTH category, PTH > 72.8 pg/mL was associated with 1.89 kg/m2 higher BMI, higher odds of morbid obesity (odds ratio: 1.66, 95% confidence interval: 1.33-2.09), and 1.67 cm greater WC. Compared with 25(OH)D < 12 ng/mL, concentrations > 35 ng/mL were associated with 1.81 kg/m2 lower BMI, lower odds of morbid obesity (odds ratio: 0.60, 95% confidence interval: 0.48-0.75), and 3.30 cm lower WC. For a PTH increase from 10 to 65 pg/mL, 25(OH)D mediated 7% of the total association with BMI and 9% with WC. Higher PTH and lower 25(OH)D were associated with BMI and WC. Exploratory decomposition suggested that circulating 25(OH)D accounted for only a small portion of the PTH-adiposity association. These findings support careful preoperative mineral-metabolism phenotyping and evaluation of abnormal PTH, but do not establish direction or causality within this framework.

articles.titulo: Resilient but Unreliable: Cross-Generational Restructuring of the Tribolium castaneum Gut Microbiome Under Contrasting Nutritional Regimes.
articles.autores: Okamoto KE, Harris EV, … Kovacs J (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Microbial communities are frequently exposed to environmental disturbances, yet recovery does not always lead to a single, predictable outcome. Distinguishing resilience, the capacity to recover following perturbation, from reliability, the predictability of that recovery, is essential for understanding microbiome dynamics. Here, we investigated cross-generational gut microbiome responses in the red flour beetle, Tribolium castaneum, a globally significant stored-product pest exposed to frequent environmental and dietary shifts. Using a four-generation experimental design (G0-G3), we examined how gut microbial communities respond to a major environmental transition from commercial to laboratory rearing, followed by dietary perturbations. The shift to laboratory conditions produced the largest change in gut microbiome composition, occurring within a single generation and exceeding the effects of dietary shifts. Following this disturbance, microbial communities stabilized across subsequent generations, consistent with strong ecological resilience. However, recovery trajectories and endpoints differed among treatments, with replicate lineages stabilizing toward multiple, partially distinct community configurations rather than a single shared state, indicating low reliability. Diet influenced overall community composition and diversity trajectories, but these effects were smaller in magnitude than the dominant generational restructuring. Together, these results show that the T. castaneum gut microbiome is resilient but not strictly reliable, stabilizing after rapid reorganization toward multiple partially distinct community configurations associated with environmental history rather than a single shared state. These findings underscore the importance of environmental context in shaping host-associated microbiomes and suggest that the capacity for rapid microbiome restructuring may contribute to the ecological success of insect pests in variable environments.

articles.titulo: Salinity acclimation induces hepatic immune-redox remodeling and intestinal mucosal adaptation in Nile tilapia: insights from multi-tissue transcriptomics and gut microbiota profiling.
articles.autores: Wang YX, Meekuan P, … Hou ZS (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Salinity fluctuation is a major challenge in aquaculture and can influence immune homeostasis and host-microbiota interactions in fish. However, the coordinated responses of multiple organs and their association with intestinal microbiota remain incompletely understood. Here, Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) were exposed to 0, 16, and 30 ppt salinity, and multi-tissue transcriptomics of the brain, intestine, and liver were integrated with hepatic antioxidant indices and intestinal microbiota profiling to investigate systemic adaptation mechanisms. Salinity exposure induced marked tissue-specific transcriptional remodeling. In the brain, differentially expressed genes were enriched in MAPK, calcium, and GnRH signaling pathways, indicating transcriptional modulation of neuroendocrine- and stress-related signaling. In the intestine, salinity mainly affected ATP metabolism, ion homeostasis, DNA replication, and cellular stress responses, indicating mucosal metabolic adjustment and stress adaptation. In the liver, high salinity enriched genes related to oxidative stress, immune processes, antigen processing and presentation, and ion homeostasis, accompanied by increased SOD and CAT activities and reduced MDA levels, indicating pronounced hepatic immunometabolic-related transcriptional responses and redox-related responses during salinity acclimation. In parallel, salinity altered intestinal microbiota structure, characterized by changes in Firmicutes, Planctomycetota, and Cetobacterium, and predicted microbial functions related to metabolism and transport. Correlation analysis further linked dominant microbial genera with host antioxidant, immune, and metabolic indicators. These findings indicate that salinity acclimation in Nile tilapia involves coordinated but tissue-specific physiological responses, characterized by intestinal metabolic and epithelial stress adaptation, hepatic immune-redox remodeling, and brain neuroendocrine-related transcriptional modulation. The salinity-responsive microbial features identified here may serve as candidate indicators of host acclimation status.

articles.titulo: Blueberry Anthocyanins Alleviate Testicular Aging in Middle-Aged Mice by Targeting Inflammaging and Reprogramming the cAMP-Wnt and Methionine-NAD+ Metabolic Axes.
articles.autores: Guo L, Zhang Z, … Zou K (10 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Emerging evidence suggests that inflammaging contributes significantly to male reproductive senescence and oxidative stress, yet safe, non-invasive interventions that act on the upstream regulatory circuitry of the spermatogonial niche remain elusive. Here we investigated the restorative potential of a high-anthocyanin Blueberry Anthocyanin Extract (BAE) in a middle-aged murine model, integrating physiological monitoring, histopathology, and paired testicular transcriptomics and metabolomics to resolve the molecular logic of BAE-mediated rejuvenation. BAE prevented age-associated physiological deterioration without detectable toxicity, reversed seminiferous tubule degeneration, and restored sperm kinematics. Mechanistically, multi-omics integration converged on three coordinated regulatory modules rather than a single pathway. First, BAE engaged adenylyl cyclase-cAMP-PKA signaling to license canonical Wnt/β-catenin activity, driving spermatogonial proliferation (PLZF, PCNA, c-Myc, Ccnd1). Second, BAE suppressed ROS-dependent IKK/NF-κBNF (p65) activation, lowering testicular and systemic TNF-α and IL-6 and resolving the pro-inflammatory niche. Third, BAE reprogrammed the methionine cycle and elevated NAD+, activating the AMPK-SIRT1-PGC1α axis while restraining leucine- and methionine-driven mTORC1 signaling, thereby coupling redox balance to cell-cycle re-entry. Collectively, these data identify BAE as a dual-action, immunometabolic modulator that simultaneously reactivates the spermatogonial proliferative program and dismantles the inflammaging circuit. By concurrently targeting the cAMP-Wnt, ROS-NF-κB, and methionine-NAD+ axes, high-anthocyanin BAE offers a mechanism-based functional-food strategy to delay male reproductive aging and preserve fertility.

articles.titulo: Novel RNA viruses and differences in viral composition between summer and winter collections of a Portuguese Drosophila suzukii population
articles.autores: Costa-Santos M, Santos C, … Hernández-Pelegrín L (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Insect-associated RNA viruses are important modulators of host physiology, immunity, and population dynamics. Factors such as host ecology, geographical niches, and seasonal variation may influence virus-host interactions and shape virome composition. Characterizing viral communities across populations and host contexts is therefore essential for understanding the ecological and evolutionary drivers of viral diversity. The spotted-wing drosophila (Drosophila suzukii), an invasive pest of soft fruits, provides an ideal system to study insect-associated viruses due to its global spread and its presence in the field throughout the year. Here, we used high-throughput RNA sequencing to characterize the RNA virome of a Portuguese population of D. suzukii, analysing flies collected at a single site in summer (July 2021) and the following winter (January 2022). We identified nine viruses, including four putative novel viruses (DsuNV1, DsuViV1, DsuPhV1, and DsuRV1) and five previously described viruses reported in D. suzukii or related Drosophila hosts. Viral detection, prevalence, and abundance differed between the two collections, with some viruses identified in only one sampling period. The observed variation highlights the dynamic nature of viral communities in natural populations and expands the known diversity of viruses associated with this economically important pest. Additionally, the differences in viral repertoires observed between sampling periods suggest that dispersal, local ecology, and seasonal factors may contribute to shaping the D. suzukii virome, providing a foundation for future studies on virus-host interactions.

articles.titulo: Multi-omics integration reveals a gut microbiota-metabolite-immune axis in PFOA-induced intestinal toxicity.
articles.autores: Wang KW, Liu W, … Huang J (10 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) is a persistent environmental contaminant associated with immunometabolic toxicity; however, its effects on the intestinal microenvironment remain incompletely understood. We integrated a murine PFOA exposure model with untargeted serum metabolomics, 16S rRNA gene sequencing, and single-cell RNA sequencing to characterize intestinal injury and explore microbiota-metabolite-immune relationships. PFOA exposure caused dose-dependent body weight loss, colon shortening, histopathological injury, disrupted epithelial junctional staining, and increased proinflammatory cytokine concentrations. It was also associated with restructuring of the gut microbiota and broad alterations in serum tryptophan-related metabolites, including a metabolomic feature putatively annotated as indole-3-propionic acid (IPA), whose normalized relative abundance was reduced. Single-cell analyses indicated remodeling of epithelial, T-cell, and fibroblast states, including enrichment of a T helper 1 (Th1)-like transcriptional program and altered fibroblast-associated inflammatory pathways. IPA supplementation partially ameliorated several PFOA-associated intestinal and inflammatory phenotypes but did not broadly normalize α-diversity, β-diversity, the relative abundance of Clostridium, or the fibroblast-associated markers examined. In polarized murine Th1 cells, IPA reduced JAK2 and STAT3 phosphorylation; this effect was partially attenuated by the AhR antagonist CH-223191, consistent with AhR-dependent restraint of JAK-STAT signaling. CellChat analysis further identified computationally inferred changes in selected CD44-associated ligand-receptor pairs between fibroblasts and Th1 cells. Collectively, these findings support a model in which PFOA-associated perturbation of microbial tryptophan metabolism and IPA-related signaling may contribute to epithelial and immune dysfunction.

articles.titulo: Metabolic-Immune Crosstalk in Colorectal Cancer: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Opportunities.
articles.autores: Lu Y, Li X, … Chu D (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major cause of cancer-related morbidity and mortality worldwide, with its progression and therapeutic resistance increasingly recognized as consequences of complex metabolic and immune interactions within the tumour microenvironment (TME). Recent advances in single-cell and spatial multi-omics technologies have enabled detailed characterisation of metabolic heterogeneity among TME components, uncovering how distinct metabolic states influence immune function and therapeutic responses. In this review, we summarize recent advances in our understanding of metabolic regulation in the CRC microenvironment, with a particular focus on how distinct immune cell populations contribute to tumour progression and immune suppression through diverse metabolic pathways. We discuss key metabolite-driven signalling networks involving lactate, short-chain fatty acids, bile acids, and amino acid derivatives, and examine how these pathways influence immune cell function and tumour-immune interactions. Furthermore, we highlight emerging therapeutic approaches targeting the metabolic-immune axis, including glutaminase inhibitors, CD36 antagonists, and combination regimens integrating metabolic intervention with immune checkpoint inhibitors. By integrating recent mechanistic discoveries with therapeutic perspectives, this review provides an updated overview of the metabolic-immune landscape in CRC and discusses potential strategies to exploit metabolic vulnerabilities for improving immunotherapy efficacy and overcoming treatment resistance.

articles.titulo: Noncanonical metabolic and immune checkpoint topography in cancer
articles.autores: Ying H, He T, … Xu D (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Tumor metabolism and immune regulation are traditionally interpreted through global metabolic reprogramming and canonical, membrane-bound immunosuppression. Emerging evidence, however, indicates that metabolic components and immune checkpoints frequently undergo subcellular spatial redistribution, generating highly localized microdomains of accumulation and specific depletion zones within tumor cells. These compartmentalized events drive noncanonical molecular functions that extend far beyond their classical roles. By reshaping epigenetic regulation, oncogenic signaling, and local protein-interaction networks, these spatial shifts influence malignant phenotypes, immune evasion, and therapeutic responses. In this review, we highlight the subcellular compartmentalization of metabolic and immune checkpoint components, alongside their corresponding localized enrichment and depletion states, and discuss their intricate interplay. We illustrate how these spatially restricted dynamics establish a highly organized layer of tumor immunometabolic crosstalk.

articles.titulo: Bistable regulation of adipocyte heterogeneity governs thermogenesis
articles.autores: Song A, Wang Y, … Wang QA (19 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Brown adipocytes (BAs) are thermogenic cells that regulate energy homeostasis, and age-related declines in thermogenesis contribute to cold sensitivity1-5. We previously identified a BA subpopulation with low UCP1 expression (hereafter, BA-L cells) that coexists with the classical, high-UCP1-expressing BAs (hereafter, BA-H cells)6. Here we show that IL-1β secreted by neutrophils and macrophages stabilizes nearby BAs in the BA-L state. Specifically, IL-1β stabilizes hexose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (H6PD) protein from degradation to ensure the generation of active glucocorticoids, which activate the glucocorticoid receptor (GR, encoded by Nr3c1) and increase the expression of its target gene, regulator of G-protein signalling 2 (Rgs2), thereby suppressing UCP1 expression. Cold exposure reduces IL-1β levels, depending on sympathetic innervation, leading to H6PD degradation and the conversion of BA-L cells to BA-H cells, thereby enhancing UCP1-dependent thermogenesis. Rising environmental temperatures trigger the opposite events. BA-specific inducible deletion of Nr3c1 during cold exposure locks these cells in the BA-H state, leading to persistent thermogenesis and increased energy expenditure days after the mice return to room temperature. Notably, IL-1β is elevated in aged brown adipose tissue, resulting in a locked low BA-H/BA-L ratio and cold intolerance. Suppressing GR in aged mice restores the BA-H/BA-L ratio, resumes thermogenesis and increases energy expenditure. Our findings reveal a spatiotemporal neuronal-immune regulation of BA heterogeneity that governs thermogenesis and offers a fundamental understanding of the mechanisms underlying increased cold sensitivity in older individuals.

articles.titulo: Dynamic reprogramming of alveolar epithelial-immune cell interactions in ARDS: from mechanisms to clinical translation.
articles.autores: Gao C, Wang Q, … Wen L (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is a life-threatening syndrome characterized by disruption of the alveolar-capillary barrier and refractory hypoxemia. Despite advances in supportive care, effective targeted therapies remain lacking. A major challenge to therapeutic success is the marked heterogeneity of ARDS, in which distinct biological mechanisms may drive different etiologies, inflammatory subphenotypes, and disease stages. Increasing evidence suggests that alveolar epithelial cells (AECs) are not merely passive targets of injury but active regulators of immune responses. Dynamic interactions between AECs and macrophages, neutrophils, and lymphocytes occur throughout the course of ARDS and contribute to inflammatory amplification, tissue repair, and aberrant remodeling. In this review, we summarize epithelial-immune interaction patterns across the inflammatory exudative, proliferative repair, and fibrotic phases of ARDS. We further discuss how disease stage transitions, immunometabolic regulation, and ARDS heterogeneity shape these interaction networks. Based on these findings, we present an AEC-centered dynamic reprogramming framework that organizes current evidence on how epithelial-immune interactions change during ARDS progression. We also discuss candidate biomarkers, approaches for clinical stage and phenotype identification, therapeutic opportunities, and current evidence limitations, aiming to provide a conceptual framework for stage-specific and precision interventions in ARDS. We further contextualize existing and controversial immunomodulatory strategies, including corticosteroids and IL-6/IL-1 blockade, within this dynamic framework to illustrate how disease stage and patient phenotype may influence therapeutic responses. Throughout the review, we distinguish evidence derived from experimental models from observational data in human ARDS and separately identify human interventional evidence and therapies supported by current clinical guidelines.

articles.titulo: EMMPRIN-mediated metabolism of monocytes promotes disease progression in a mouse model of multiple sclerosis
articles.autores: Kaushik DK, Das A, … Yong VW (13 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Monocytes and monocyte-derived macrophages are increasingly recognized as key contributors to the initiation and progression of inflammatory conditions, in part through metabolic reprogramming that drives pathogenic inflammatory phenotypes. However, the upstream mechanisms that coordinate these early metabolic transitions in multiple sclerosis (MS) remain largely undefined. We previously identified extracellular matrix metalloproteinase inducer (EMMPRIN/CD147), a chaperone of monocarboxylate transporter 4 (MCT4), as a regulator of lactate efflux and glycolysis-dependent activation in murine macrophages. Here, we investigate the role of EMMPRIN in circulating CCR2+ monocytes during experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE), a mouse model for MS. Using the newly generated CCR2CreERT2:EMMPRINfl/fl (CCR2:EMMP-/-) mice, we demonstrate that presymptomatic deletion of EMMPRIN prevents or significantly attenuates clinical disability and is associated with a marked reduction in CNS infiltration by CD45+ leukocytes, including macrophages and T cells. Single cell RNA-sequencing of blood monocytes during pre-onset EAE, combined with proteomic profiling of bone marrow-derived macrophages from CCR2:EMMP-/- mice, reveals coordinated metabolic reprogramming characterized by reduced glycolytic activity, enhanced mitochondrial electron transport, and increased fatty acid oxidation. These data identify EMMPRIN-mediated lactate export as a pivotal regulator of immunometabolic programming in monocytes and monocyte-derived macrophages and implicate this pathway as an upstream driver of early neuroinflammatory pathology in MS. Targeting this pathway during presymptomatic phases may therefore represent a promising strategy to prevent disease progression by modulating early inflammatory metabolism.

articles.titulo: DNA Methylation in Bovine Mastitis: Regulatory Mechanisms, Shared Networks, and Translational Prospects.
articles.autores: Dwivedi S, Kumar A (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Bovine mastitis is a multifactorial inflammatory disease shaped by interactions among host genetics, physiological state, environmental exposure, management, and pathogen characteristics. DNA methylation is an important regulatory mechanism linking these factors with changes in mammary immunity, metabolism, and secretory function. This review synthesizes evidence from methylome and integrated methylome-transcriptome studies in blood cells, mammary tissue, and milk somatic cells. Mastitis associated with Staphylococcus aureus, Escherichia coli, Streptococcus uberis, Staphylococcus chromogenes, Streptococcus agalactiae, and Prototheca spp. shows distinct but overlapping methylation changes affecting cytokine signaling, leukocyte recruitment, antigen processing, epithelial integrity, and mammary metabolism. Recurrent methylation-expression relationships across studies suggest shared regulatory features despite pathogen- and tissue-specific responses. The review further examines the influence of nutrition, heat stress, and physiological state, while addressing key interpretative challenges, including analytical thresholds, platform heterogeneity, genomic context, cellular composition, and limited longitudinal validation. Emerging applications include methylation-based biomarkers, integrated disease-monitoring panels, epigenetically informed breeding, targeted epigenome editing, and trained-immunity-based interventions. Translation will require harmonized analytical approaches, independent multiherd validation, and functional confirmation of candidate loci across populations and disease contexts. Overall, DNA methylation provides a mechanistic framework for understanding mastitis as a dynamic host-pathogen-environment interaction and for developing biologically informed strategies for disease management.

articles.titulo: Premature immune aging in obesity: a testable framework linking immunosenescence, metaflammation, and multiorgan dysfunction
articles.autores: Sulaiman SH, Omer RA, … Barzani HAH (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Obesity is a chronic immunometabolic disorder associated with alterations in biological aging pathways and increased risks of type 2 diabetes mellitus, cardiovascular disease, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, chronic kidney disease, neurodegeneration, and cancer. Obesity and chronological aging share several characteristics, including low-grade inflammation, cellular senescence, mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, epigenetic alterations, and immune remodeling. However, these similarities do not necessarily establish accelerated biological immune aging. This review critically evaluates obesity-associated immunosenescence, metaflammation, and multiorgan dysfunction by examining supporting and conflicting findings, alternative explanations, methodological limitations, and therapeutic evidence. Although experimental and observational studies report alterations in lymphocyte differentiation, innate immune function, inflammatory signaling, and selected biological-age markers, these findings are not uniformly observed across immune-cell populations, tissues, or metabolic phenotypes. Metabolically healthy obesity, tissue-dependent epigenetic aging, and differences between human and animal findings challenge the interpretation of obesity as a universal accelerator of immunosenescence. Furthermore, chronological age, cytomegalovirus infection, sex-related differences, adiposity distribution, and metabolic comorbidities complicate attributing immune alterations specifically to obesity. The proposed immunosenescence-metaflammation-multiorgan dysfunction framework therefore remains a testable mechanistic hypothesis rather than an established causal pathway. Although immune-cell phenotypes, epigenetic clocks, inflammatory mediators, and multi-omics signatures may help characterize obesity-associated immune dysfunction, their specificity, longitudinal validity, and clinical utility remain insufficiently established. Nutritional interventions, exercise, bariatric surgery, and pharmacological treatments can improve selected metabolic and inflammatory outcomes, but these improvements do not necessarily demonstrate sustained reversal of biological immune aging. By critically comparing supportive evidence with contradictory observations and unresolved causal relationships, this review identifies the principal limitations of current mechanistic, biomarker, and therapeutic research. Future studies should prioritize longitudinal immune profiling, direct functional assessment, tissue- and sex-specific analyses, causal validation, and controlled interventions incorporating validated immune-aging endpoints to determine whether premature immune aging is a measurable and therapeutically modifiable consequence of obesity.

articles.titulo: ASCENT: a tensor-oriented approach to population-scale agent-based simulation
articles.autores: Mahmood I, Wickramasooriya S, … Wooldridge M (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Agent-based models (ABMs) offer a compelling framework for simulating complex systems but scale poorly with conventional software execution paradigms. When modelling millions of interacting agents with complex lifecycles and spatial dynamics, conventional ABMs encounter severe computational bottlenecks, e.g., from memory fragmentation and loop-based state updates. We introduce ASCENT (agent-based simulation using computationally efficient nested tensors), a tensor-oriented approach that reformulates agent state, interactions, and transitions as tensor programs, which enables population-level vectorised computation on commodity GPU hardware. ASCENT supports heterogeneous agent attributes, stochastic state transitions, spatially explicit movement, and machine-learning-driven behaviours, while substantially reducing the traditional trade-off between expressiveness and computational scale. Applied to modelling of gene drive mosquito dynamics on Príncipe Island, ASCENT can simulate millions of individual agents with full lifecycle, genetic inheritance, and spatial dispersal fidelity, demonstrating that a single strategically placed release achieves 95% allele prevalence within approximately 73 days. The emergent Allee effect threshold at ∼ 300 individuals further validates the model's ecological fidelity. These results demonstrate that our tensor-oriented reformulation enables population-scale agent-based simulation without sacrificing behavioural richness.

articles.titulo: Non-classical Mullins-Sekerka instability during mineralization at gas-liquid interfaces
articles.autores: Wegner L, Santoso R, … Poonoosamy J (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Diffusion-driven morphological instability, described by Mullins-Sekerka theory, predicts amplification of interfacial perturbations and wavelength selection for idealized sharp interfaces. However, natural systems rarely satisfy these assumptions. Here, we investigate barite mineralization on the growing interface of CO[Formula: see text] gas bubbles using 3D focused ion beam scanning electron microscopy (FIB-SEM) tomography, quantitative surface analysis and reactive transport modelling. Bubble morphologies exhibit diffusion-driven instability, with dominant modes consistent with Mullins-Sekerka predictions. However, the interface violates key assumptions of the classical framework; it is porous, transport active, and evolves in pore space confinement, while crystallization proceeds via heterogenous nucleation, producing a polycrystalline interface. We show that diffusion-driven instability persists under these conditions but with modified mode selection, defining a non-classical Mullins-Sekerka regime for gas-liquid interface mineralization. Such dynamics influence pore structure evolution and transport pathways in the subsurface environment.

articles.titulo: Serum isthmin-1 levels in chronic hepatitis B: association with viral replication and hepatic dysfunction
articles.autores: Öner P, Şenol FF, … Algül S (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a major global health problem, underscoring the need for biomarkers that reflect viral replication and liver function. Isthmin-1 (ISM-1), an immunometabolic adipokine, has not been adequately studied in chronic HBV infection. This study evaluated serum ISM-1 levels in patients with chronic HBV to assess its potential as a complementary marker of viral activity and hepatic dysfunction.
In this cross-sectional study, 100 patients with histologically mild chronic hepatitis B and 60 healthy controls were enrolled. Serum ISM-1 levels were measured using a commercial enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) kit alongside comprehensive virological and biochemical assessments.
Serum ISM-1 concentrations were significantly lower in patients with chronic HBV than in healthy controls (102.74 ± 15.64 vs. 194.62 ± 187.59 pg/mL; p < 0.001). ISM-1 levels demonstrated a significant downward trend as HBV DNA categories increased (p = 0.001), indicating an inverse relationship with viral replication. Multiple linear regression identified direct bilirubin as a positive independent predictor of ISM-1 levels. ROC analysis showed moderate overall performance (AUC = 0.656); the marker exhibited a remarkably high sensitivity (97.0%) but limited specificity (38.7%).
Serum ISM-1 levels are significantly reduced in chronic HBV infection and are inversely associated with viral replication. The positive correlation with direct bilirubin may reflect an adaptive cellular response to hepatocellular stress rather than simple dysfunction. Despite its limited specificity, the high sensitivity of ISM-1 suggests that it could be a valuable complementary tool for monitoring disease progression and viral status in clinical practice.

articles.titulo: High-throughput fabrication of nanofibrous yarns produced by alternating-current electrospinning
articles.autores: Mikule J, Friedrich O, … Lukas D (15 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Nanofiber yarns offer unique opportunities for developing next-generation flexible materials that combine nanoscale functionality with macroscopic structural integrity. Their high surface-to-volume ratio, fine open porosity, and fibrous morphology enable applications in tissue engineering, drug delivery, filtration, sensors, energy storage, and functional textiles. However, the transition of nanofiber yarn technology from laboratory to industrial scale has been limited by low productivity and poor control over morphology, linear density, twist, and tensile strength. Here, we report a simple and robust method with strong scale-up potential for the continuous production of 100% nanofiber yarns using high-throughput needleless and collectorless alternating-current (AC) electrospinning. A plume of nanofibers generated from a rotating disc spinning-electrode is continuously deposited on a rotating drum and withdrawn through a spinning triangle, where a twirling device imparts controlled twist. Using this setup, nanofiber yarns composed of poly(vinyl butyral) (PVB), poly(ε-caprolactone) (PCL), polyamide 46 (PA46), and poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) were produced at speeds up to 55 m min⁻¹ with a 200 mm disc spinning-electrode. Scanning electron microscopy revealed densely packed nanofibrils within the yarn cross-sections and a dominant pore size around 1 µm. The yarns were braided and woven into scaffolds supporting cell adhesion and proliferation. This high-performance alternating-current electrospinning approach effectively bridges the gap between electrospun fibers-whose two of three characteristic dimensions reside in the nanoscale-and macroscopic textile manufacturing, thereby enabling a practical and scalable pathway for the industrial production of nanofiber yarns for biomedical and advanced material applications.

articles.titulo: The gut-disc axis in intervertebral disc degeneration: microbial metabolites, immunometabolic remodeling, and regulated cell death
articles.autores: Wu H, Yuan D, … Liu S (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IDD) involves interactions among mechanical injury, inflammation, and metabolic dysfunction. The proposed gut-disc axis extends this framework to intestinal microbial signals, but the strength and tissue relevance of the supporting evidence vary considerably. This narrative review examines whether microbial metabolites could influence IDD through pyroptosis, a gasdermin-mediated form of lytic regulated cell death, and ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death driven by lipid peroxidation. We distinguish human microbial associations, experimental findings in disc tissues, mechanisms demonstrated in other organs, and computational predictions. Selected microbial metabolites regulate inflammatory and antioxidant pathways in non-disc models, whereas disc studies establish the relevance of mitochondrial dysfunction, iron handling, and local metabolite-dependent protein modifications. These findings support mechanistic hypotheses but do not establish that defined gut-derived metabolites reach the disc and causally regulate either death program. We also assess microbiome-directed interventions and local therapeutic strategies, emphasizing that efficacy against a downstream disc pathway does not demonstrate a microbial initiating mechanism. Clinical intervention evidence remains limited and does not establish structural disease modification. Translation requires verified metabolite exposure, cell-specific target engagement, functional validation of cell death, and longitudinal assessment of imaging, pain, and disability. This evidence-based distinction provides a framework for prioritizing testable gut-disc mechanisms and clinically relevant interventions.

articles.titulo: Dynamics of Mitochondrial Structure, Biogenesis and Function in Skeletal Muscle of Critically Ill Patients
articles.autores: Wickert A, Grunow JJ, … Fielitz J (12 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
To define the timing and phenotype of mitochondrial ultrastructural remodeling and electron transport chain (ETC) function in skeletal muscle during early critical illness.
Secondary analysis of a prospective observational study with serial muscle biopsies.
Adult ICU.
Thirty-three mechanically ventilated ICU patients (median age, 49 yr; 27% women) with Sequential Organ Failure Assessment greater than or equal to 9 on three consecutive days; skeletal muscle biopsies of the vastus lateralis muscle at ICU day 5 (n = 29) and day 15 (n = 22). Healthy subjects served as controls.
None.
Vastus lateralis biopsies were analyzed by electron microscopy with stereology, quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR), Western blotting, and spectrophotometric ETC enzyme assays (reported per tissue weight and normalized to citrate synthase [CS]). Intact mitochondrial profiles were reduced vs. controls (fold change vs. controls: day 5, 0.24 [0.18-0.34]; p = 0.039 and day 15, 0.20 [0.16-0.33]; p = 0.011) and disturbed profiles increased (day 5, 5.62 [3.20-7.17]; p < 0.001 and day 15, 5.20 [3.67-6.36]; p = 0.001), with reduced volume density of intact mitochondria (day 5, 0.33 [0.20-0.49]; p = 0.009 and day 15, 0.32 [0.21-0.50]; p = 0.005). Inner mitochondrial membrane surface-to-volume ratio was reduced at day 5 (0.69 [0.49-0.89]; p = 0.022) and remained unchanged at day 15. Complex III tissue activity was reduced at day 5 (85.6 [22.1-133.3] vs. 151.4 [100.5-205.0]; p = 0.015) and day 15 (50.5 [36.0-69.8]; p = 0.001), remaining reduced after CS normalization (day 5, 0.83 [0.34-1.49]; p = 0.040 and day 15, 0.87 [0.65-0.93]; p = 0.007). Complex IV activity remained reduced before and after CS normalization at both time points (all p < 0.001). CS activity declined by day 15 (56.3 [52.7-65.1] vs. 95.6 [80.1-133.0]; p = 0.001 and day 15 vs. day 5; p = 0.041). qRT-PCR and Western blot supported reduced ETC components and altered biogenesis signaling.
Skeletal muscle mitochondrial ultrastructure is altered by ICU day 5 and remains abnormal at day 15, with persistent complex III/IV dysfunction after CS normalization. These findings define an early sustained mitochondrial remodeling phenotype in skeletal muscle during critical illness.
